extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into an OS command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via the 'host' parameter (e.g., 'host=127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd').

User-supplied request body (optionally base64-decoded) is deserialized using pickle.loads(), which can execute arbitrary code. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to achieve remote code execution.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This enables Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code via Jinja2 template expressions (e.g., {{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}).

XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, parsing user-supplied request.body. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, allowing file disclosure and server-side request forgery.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-supplied JSON payload is used directly as a MongoDB query filter in find_one(). An attacker can pass MongoDB query operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}) to bypass filters or extract unintended data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: User input from request.GET['lane'] or request.POST['lane'] is passed directly to redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL with 'lane=https://evil.com' to redirect users to malicious sites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Hardcoded verifier codes ("north": "4812", "south": "5930") are embedded directly in source code. These are effectively authentication secrets that cannot be rotated without code changes.

The get_client_ip() function trusts the X-Forwarded-For header without validation. An attacker can spoof their IP address by setting this header, which is used for audit logging. This can be exploited to bypass IP-based restrictions or corrupt audit trails.

The admin_user_toggle view performs a state-changing operation (enabling/disabling user accounts) via GET request. GET requests are not protected by Django's CSRF middleware, making this vulnerable to CSRF attacks. An attacker can trick an admin into visiting a crafted URL to disable user accounts.

The assignment_status view changes assignment status via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick an instructor into visiting a crafted URL to change assignment statuses (e.g., publish draft assignments or archive active ones).

The discussion_moderate view changes thread status (pin, lock, hide) via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick a moderator into visiting a crafted URL to lock or hide discussion threads.
The release_grade view releases grades via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick an instructor into visiting a crafted URL to prematurely release grades to students.

The request_resubmission view changes submission status via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick a grader into visiting a crafted URL to request resubmission on a student's work.
CSV user import creates accounts with a default password of 'changeme123' when no password is provided in the CSV. This is a weak, easily guessable password that leaves imported accounts vulnerable.

The SignUpForm includes a 'role' ChoiceField with all role options including 'school_admin'. This allows any user registering via the signup page to set their own role to school_admin, granting full administrative privileges. The view at core/views.py:87-98 saves the form directly without overriding the role.

The Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded insecure default value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' used when the environment variable is not set. This key is used for cryptographic signing of sessions and CSRF tokens. If deployed without setting the environment variable, an attacker can forge sessions and CSRF tokens.

The DATABASE_URL has a hardcoded default containing database credentials 'lms_user:lms_pass'. If the environment variable is not set, these credentials are used, potentially exposing the database in production.
